result_text:
Template literals are now normalized like the other string literals when units are compared for duplication. The `codeanalyzer` module tests pass (`mvn -q -o -pl codeanalyzer test`, no failures). I didn't run an end-to-end duplication report on JavaScript files. The new test only covers the normalization step, not a full unit-duplicates run.

- **Change:** in `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.extraCleanContent`, I added `cleanedContent.replaceAll("`.*?`", "``")` right after the single-quote rule. `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` and `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` now clean to the same text. A difference in the code outside the literal still keeps the units apart.
- **Test:** `cleanContentTemplateLiterals` in `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest` checks that the two literals clean identically.
- **Multi-line templates:** the match is single-line, like the existing `"` and `'` rules, so a template literal spanning several lines is not normalized.
- **Other language extractors:** `extraCleanContent` is shared by the other C-style extractors, so they also get the backtick rule.
